title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
quote: We found that only flies that expressed CsChrimson in the GF and had been fed retinal displayed takeoff behaviors
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron GF and states it is 'also known in the literature as DNp01'; GF is a listed synonym of DNp01 (synonyms.csv, unambiguous).
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 300 ms pulse, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single stimulation per fly
sensory_condition: tethered to tungsten wire, holding a small piece of Kimwipe (no ground contact)
coordination_notes: middle leg extension, wing depression and flight initiation (Fig 2A)
penetrance: about 83% of experimental flies escaped (Fig 2B bar); 0% in non-retinal and wild-type controls
notes: Single takeoff movement (leg extension), coded 'no' for leg rhythm per PROTOCOL sec. 3. Paper calls the driver 'highly specific'. Penetrance read from Fig 2B bar height.

title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
quote: We found that flies expressing CsChrimson in neurons labeled by this line displayed freezing behavior at a high probability
mapping_basis: Paper says SS1540 labels the DN pair 'called DNp09' (Namiki nomenclature, line from Namiki 2018); kit lists SS01540 and the name DNp09 as AMBIGUOUS (DNp09; DNp71 via hemibrain name); the paper's Namiki-system naming supports MANC DNp09.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 300 ms pulse, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single stimulation per fly
sensory_condition: tethered to tungsten wire, no tarsal contact; fly moving its legs (grooming/struggling) before stimulation
other_cell_types: other (unnamed) neurons labelled by SS1540-split-Gal4, suggested by the authors to cause freezing
coordination_notes: complete interruption of appendage movement during and after light (Fig 3A)
penetrance: about 62% of retinal-fed experimental flies froze vs about 20% of non-retinal-fed (Fig 3B bars)
n_flies_note: n = 80 retinal-fed experimental flies; 79 non-retinal; 24 per wild-type control (Fig 3B)
notes: Paper states freezing may come from other SS1540 neurons rather than DNp09 ('other labeled neurons in SS1540-split-Gal4 are responsible for the freezing phenotype' [citing Bidaye 2020]) and did not observe increased locomotion, attributing this to tethering without tarsal contact. Line written 'SS1540' in paper = SS01540 (VT023490-p65ADZp; R38F04-ZpGAL4DBD).

title: Cell body clustering drives gap junction-mediated synchronous activity in command neurons
source_locator: Main text, 'Hunchback is required in MDNs for backward walking'; Fig. 1C (control)
quote: In control animals, when adult MDNs are optogenetically activated, the animals walk backwards (Fig. 1C)
mapping_basis: Paper name 'MDN' (Moonwalker Descending Neuron) is the MANC type name.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED from above, 5 s per trial, >=10 s inter-trial interval
sensory_condition: single fly in a 1 mL serological pipette
n_flies_note: about 12 control flies (dots in Fig. 1C); n not stated in text
notes: Control genotype: UAS-CsChrimson.mVenus; VT50600.p65AD/+; VT44845.Gal4DBD/UAS-Luc RNAi. Net backward distance scored blind from video, no leg tracking, so confidence medium (backward walking coded yes for all legs per sec. 3). Hb-RNAi in MDN abolished backward walking (net forward); knockdown conditions not recorded separately because the neuron itself is genetically altered. Driver written 'VT50600' in the paper (kit MDN-1 is VT50660-x-VT44845; probably a typo); the strain list also mentions SS03131.
